upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Google Ads Specialist — Paid Search Strategy & Account Architecture
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Hello!

We are managing paid search for a national B2B environmental services company: 1,000+ employees, 30+ locations across the U.S., PE-backed. The company recently unified multiple acquired brands under a single identity, and the Google Ads infrastructure hasn't caught up yet.

We have three active Google Ads brand accounts that are currently self-competing in overlapping geographies, running without proper negative keyword architecture, and operating on conversion data that's been inflated by duplicate tracking events for years. The foundation needs to be fixed before anything else can be built on top of it.

I'm looking for someone who can come in, understand the structural problems quickly, and execute with minimal hand-holding. This is not a campaign management role. This is diagnostic and architectural work first then ongoing optimization once the foundation is clean.

What the work looks like:

The immediate priorities are:

1. Complete a keyword ownership map across three brand accounts, assigning keyword territories by account and geography to eliminate internal competition

2. Deploy a comprehensive negative keyword architecture (800+ terms) segmented by match type across all three accounts

3. Finalize geo-targeting restructure to give each account clean geographic boundaries with zero overlap

4. Run a full campaign architecture QA once all changes are implemented

From there, the work shifts into Month 2 and Month 3 territory: Customer Match audience activation, Performance Max readiness assessment, and ongoing optimization as clean conversion data starts accumulating.

What we need from you:

1. Deep familiarity with Google Ads account structure: campaigns, ad groups, match types, negative keyword lists, shared libraries, geo-targeting settings

2. Experience managing multiple accounts under a single MCC, specifically identifying and resolving cross-account keyword conflict
Comfort working from search term reports and keyword data to build negative keyword architecture grounded in actual account history, not generic lists

3. Ability to produce clean, documented deliverables, not just make changes and move on
Understanding of conversion tracking and how duplicate events distort performance data

4. B2B experience preferred. 

5. Environmental services, construction, or industrial services background is a plus but not required

How we work:

1. We can give direction but we expect you to bring your own thinking. If you see something or new opportunities, say so.

2. Weekly async updates are required: what changed, what was done, what's needed for next steps.

Logistics:

1. This is a part-time hourly engagement, roughly 10–15 hours per month once the initial remediation work is done. The first month will likely run heavier given the catch-up work needed. 

2. Rate range is $35–$45/hr depending on experience.

3. I'm looking to get started immediately. If you're available to hit the ground running this week, flag that in your cover letter.

To confirm you've read this post, include the phrase "clean architecture" at the top of your cover letter.

To apply:

1. Tell me specifically about a time you diagnosed and resolved cross-account keyword conflict or self-competition in Google Ads. 

2. What was the setup, what did you find, and what did you do about it? 

Generic cover letters won't be considered.
questions: Describe a time you identified and resolved self-competition between sibling brand accounts in Google Ads. What was the root cause and how did you fix it?
Two sibling brand accounts are running in the same metro area. Neither has identical keyword strings. Is there self-competition? How do you diagnose it and what do you do about it?

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Lead Intelligence & Territory Routing System
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Lead Intelligence & Territory Routing System


End-to-end AI pipeline for automated B2B lead enrichment, scoring, and geo-spatial routing



BACKGROUND
A B2B SaaS company receives approximately 200 inbound leads per day from a web form. Each lead record contains: company name, website URL, country, city, a free-text message, and contact email. Today, a human manually opens each lead, visits the company website, estimates product fit, and assigns the lead to a sales representative. This process consumes 3–4 hours of daily manual effort and introduces routing inconsistencies. You are hired to automate this pipeline entirely.


OBJECTIVE

Design and build an end-to-end automated pipeline that: ingests raw leads, enriches each record using an LLM, scores leads for sales fit, routes them to the correct representative based on geo-territory rules, writes results to a structured output, and monitors itself with alerts on failure.

PIPELINE SPECIFICATION

1      Ingestion Layer
Accept leads via webhook or by polling a Google Sheet / CSV. Normalize field names, validate required fields, and deduplicate incoming records before passing them downstream.

2	LLM Enrichment
For each lead, use an LLM to: infer the company industry, employee size tier (SMB / Mid-Market / Enterprise), and an ICP fit score from 0–100 based on the company website and free-text message. Extract intent signals from the message. Generate a one-sentence internal summary for the sales representative.

3	Geo-Spatial Routing
Map each lead's city/country to a defined sales territory using the provided territory config (JSON). Assign the correct representative. Handle edge cases explicitly: unmapped regions, international leads outside defined territories, and records with missing location data.

4	Scoring & Prioritisation
Combine ICP fit score, intent signals, and company size into a normalised final lead score (0–100). Flag any lead with a final score ≥ 75 as high-priority and trigger an immediate Slack notification to the assigned representative.

5	Output & Storage
Write fully enriched, scored, and routed leads to a Google Sheet or Airtable base. Each row must contain: all original fields, all enrichment fields, assigned representative, final score, priority flag, and ISO timestamp.

6	Monitoring & Alerting
Log each pipeline run: total leads processed, error count, average score, and high-priority count. Send a daily digest summary. If the pipeline encounters a fatal error, dispatch a Slack alert within 5 minutes.


SAMPLE DATA PROVIDED TO CANDIDATE

20 mock leads (CSV)  –  Includes: clean leads, leads with missing city, duplicate entries, leads with vague or ambiguous messages, and one intentional international edge case outside any defined territory.
Territory config (JSON)  –  5 sales representatives each assigned to a set of countries or regions. Contains intentional gaps — candidate must decide and document how unmapped territories are handled.

REQUIRED DELIVERABLES

Working pipeline	Runnable end-to-end. Must process all 20 sample leads without crashing.
Architecture document	One-page explanation of design decisions, tool choices, and tradeoffs made.
Output sheet	Enriched Google Sheet or Airtable base with all 20 leads processed and scored correctly.
Error log	Document what failed, why, and how it was handled. A blank log is a red flag.


EVALUATION CRITERIA

LLM prompt design	Are prompts structured and output-controlled? Do they handle ambiguous inputs gracefully?
Geo-spatial handling	Is routing correct? Are missing-city and unknown-country cases documented and handled?
Error resilience	Does the pipeline fail gracefully? Are retries, fallbacks, or dead-letter queues present?
Code / workflow quality	Is the implementation readable, modular, and maintainable by another developer?
Decision transparency	Does the architecture doc explain why choices were made, not just what was built?
Output data quality	Are scores reasonable? Is rep assignment correct? Are summaries useful to a sales rep?


TECHNOLOGY STACK

The candidate is free to choose any stack. Typical approaches include n8n, Make, Zapier, Python with LangChain, OpenAI API, Nominatim or Google Maps for geo-lookup, Airtable, Google Sheets API, Slack webhooks, or FastAPI. Stack choice is part of the evaluation — the candidate must justify why they selected their tools.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: Data Forensics Analyst — Privacy & Ad-Tech Litigation
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
We build and run consumer-protection litigation campaigns — mass arbitration and class actions targeting unlawful website tracking, undisclosed data sharing, and broken consent. The evidence that makes or breaks those campaigns is technical: what a website actually transmits, to whom, when, and whether the user ever meaningfully agreed.

You will produce that evidence. Specifically, you'll author defensible, reproducible forensic reports documenting third-party tracker behavior and consent mechanisms on consumer websites and apps — the kind of report a litigation team can build a demand letter, complaint, or expert declaration on top of, and that holds up when opposing counsel pushes back.

This is a facts role, not a legal-conclusions role. You document precisely what the technology does and preserve the proof. Our attorneys characterize it under CIPA, VPPA, the multi-state wiretap stack, and UDTP statutes. The cleaner the line you hold between "here is what fired and what it carried" and "here is what that means legally," the more useful your work is.

## What you'll produce

Reports in the mold of our existing work product — e.g., a tracker-and-consent analysis of a travel-booking site, or a pixel-history reconstruction of a lending site. A typical report includes:

- An executive summary stating, in plain terms, what data went where and whether consent was obtained
- A methodology section detailed enough that a third party can reproduce the capture
- Technical findings: trackers detected, data fields transmitted, sensitivity classification, and the raw request payloads that prove it
- A consent-mechanism analysis: what the CMP did or didn't do, and when
- A preserved, hash-verified evidence appendix with a file manifest and independent verification steps

Each report is a standalone evidentiary artifact: case reference, version, classification, analyst attribution, UTC timestamps, and a chain of evidence that survives scrutiny.

## What you'll do

- Capture network traffic at the protocol level (Chrome DevTools Protocol / HAR) and via headless and headed browser automation (Playwright, Chromium, Brave), across authenticated and unauthenticated sessions, with clean-profile baselines and controlled geo/VPN conditions
- Detect and decode third-party trackers — Meta Pixel, Google Ads/DoubleClick/Floodlight, Microsoft UET, The Trade Desk, Adobe/demdex, Criteo, TikTok, AdRoll, Impact Radius, Heap, and others — and explain exactly what each parameter carries
- Identify transmitted PII and persistent identifiers (account IDs, session GUIDs, `fbp`/`auiddc`/ECID, listing/application IDs) and classify sensitivity
- Read the consent layer: CMP initialization state and timing (e.g., OneTrust SDK load vs. `window.OneTrust`/`OptanonActiveGroups` state), consent cookies, and platform consent flags (`coo`, `cdl`, `npa`, `cdb`) that independently corroborate whether consent existed at transmission time
- Reverse out tag-manager firing logic (e.g., Tealium `utag.js` load conditions) to show what gates a pixel — URL path, event, or an actual consent check
- Reconstruct historical tracker deployment using the Wayback Machine and archived configs, building dated timelines of pixel IDs, events, and consent posture
- Inspect cookies (1st- vs 3rd-party, persistence, purpose), CSP whitelists, source maps, and SDK/API transmissions
- Preserve evidence rigorously: hash-verified captures, raw payloads keyed to HAR entry numbers, screenshots, and copy-paste verification commands (e.g., `curl` against an archived asset)
- Write clearly for a legal audience and stand behind your findings; support attorneys preparing declarations or responding to challenges

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: B2B Marketing Site Designer & Developer
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
TL;DR
We are rebuilding kelvin.ai as a marketing site designed for two audiences: the human buyer who scans and forms an impression in under a minute, and the AI agent doing buyer research on their behalf. (Plain English: we build software that helps oil refineries, power plants, and industrial facilities detect problems faster, decide what to do, and prove it worked.) We want a clean, modern, technically serious site that reads well to both. If you have built B2B marketing sites for technical companies and you have thought about how AI agents read and summarize web content, we want to hear from you.

About Kelvin
Kelvin is the System of Action for the Physical World. We build governed agents that close the loop in industrial operations: detecting events, recommending action, and proving impact on real plants. We are a Series B, venture-backed company with paying customers and a strong product story. Our current marketing site does not match the substance of the product, and that is the gap we are hiring to close.

The Project
Rebuild kelvin.ai as a marketing site that is legible to two audiences.
The first audience is human. Industrial buyers, executives, and operators who scan, click, and form an impression in under a minute. They need to know what we do, who it is for, and what makes us different. Trust beats persuasion. Specifics beat adjectives.
The second audience is AI agents. Buyer research is increasingly happening through ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and similar tools. When someone asks an agent to compare us against three competitors, the agent reads our site and writes the summary. That summary is now part of our sales motion whether we designed for it or not. The new site has to read well to a model the same way it reads well to a person.
Most marketing sites are built only for the first audience. We want both.

Scope of Work
1. Information architecture and content scaffolding. Five to seven pages total: home, what we do, who it is for, customers, company, contact, plus a customer-story template page. We will supply copy and brand direction.
2. Design and front-end build. Clean, modern, brand-aligned. Visual style is closer to Linear, Stripe, or Vercel than to a typical industrial-tech site. Brand palette and typography supplied (Proxima Nova, brand blue, teal accent).
3. Two-audience implementation. Server-side rendered or statically generated so content is visible to crawlers and agents. Semantic HTML. Structured data (Schema.org) on key claim blocks. Clean URLs. Proper sitemap, robots.txt, and Open Graph metadata. Optional but valued: an llms.txt file summarizing site structure for agent consumption.
4. Customer-story template. One standalone page built as a reusable pattern for future testimonials. Designed to be parsed as a discrete piece of content with named customer, outcome, and metric.
5. CMS or content workflow. Either headless CMS (Sanity, Contentful, or similar) or a markdown-based content workflow that lets our team edit copy without touching code. Your call, with a short rationale.
6. Performance and accessibility. Lighthouse scores in the green across the board. WCAG AA at minimum.
7. Handoff. Repo we own, documented setup, and a one-page README that lets us swap copy and ship new pages without coming back to you.

Technical Requirements
-Modern static site generator or React-based framework. Next.js, Astro, or similar.
-Deployment to Vercel, Netlify, or comparable host (final hosting decision is open).
-Git-based workflow. We own the repo on day one.
-TypeScript preferred but not required.
-No client-side JavaScript dependency for primary content. The page has to render correctly to a crawler with JS disabled.

Required Experience
-Three or more B2B marketing sites you can point to as your own work. Industrial, technical, or AI-adjacent is a plus, but more important is that the sites read as serious and substantive.
-Demonstrable understanding of SEO fundamentals, structured data, and how AI agents read and summarize web content. We are building this site to influence what LLMs say about Kelvin when a buyer asks them to compare industrial AI vendors. Familiarity with generative engine optimization (GEO) or equivalent thinking is a meaningful differentiator here.
-Comfortable working from supplied copy and a brand system rather than designing brand from scratch. A prior design pass and internal brand review have already been completed. You will be building from existing direction, not starting cold.
-Self-manages the project. We are a small team. We expect you to set milestones, surface blockers before they become problems, and not require daily check-ins. Updates in writing, on a cadence you propose at kickoff.
-Communicates in writing well. We work async and value clarity over volume.

Nice to Have
-Experience auditing how a company currently appears in LLM-generated responses (e.g. querying ChatGPT or Perplexity for vendor comparisons and measuring what comes back). Bonus if you have done this and changed something on a site as a result.
-Familiarity with industrial, manufacturing, oil and gas, or process-industry audiences.
-Experience with motion or micro-interactions used sparingly (we are not looking for a flashy site, but small moments of polish help).
-Comfort building a customer-story template that holds up across many future entries.

Timeline
-Project kickoff: within two weeks of award.
-Design and scope confirmation: 1 week from kickoff.
-First design review: within 1–2 weeks of kickoff.
-First version live: 4–6 weeks from kickoff.
-Two rounds of revision included.
If your typical project timeline is 8+ weeks, this is not the right fit.

Budget
This is a fixed-price project. We are targeting a total in the $3,500–$5,000 range, based on an estimated 80–100 hours at $35–$50/hr. Please include a specific price in your proposal. Applicants significantly outside this range will not be reviewed.

How to Apply
Please include in your proposal:
1. Two or three links to B2B marketing sites you built and led the front-end on. A one-line note on what your role was on each.
2. A two-to-four-sentence response to this question: How would you make a marketing site read well to both a human reader and an AI agent doing buyer research? We will read this answer carefully. Generic answers will not move forward. Take a look at kelvin.ai as it exists today. In 2–3 sentences, what would you change first and why?
3. Your proposed stack and CMS, plus one sentence on why.
4. A rough estimate of timeline and price for the scope above.

Proposals without a specific answer to question 2 will not be reviewed. We are looking for someone who has actually thought about this, not someone who can copy our brief back to us.
Posted by Kelvin. For questions, message us through Upwork.

We run a driving school based in Canada and we're looking for a Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) expert to audit our website and tell us exactly where we stand inside AI search platforms.
We've noticed that when potential students search for driving schools in our area using ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, and Copilot, we either don't show up at all or get represented inaccurately. Our competitors are appearing — we're not. We want to fix that.
We're not looking for a generic SEO audit. Traditional Google rankings are a separate topic. This is specifically about how AI-powered search engines see, cite, and recommend our brand.
What We Need
A complete GEO audit of our site with a real action plan we can execute. We will share the website URL once we connect.
Specifically:

AI visibility test — query our brand and relevant searches (e.g., "best driving school in [our city]", "where to learn driving in [our area]", "Canada driving lessons") across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, and Copilot. Document where we appear, where we don't, and how we're represented (or misrepresented).
Competitor benchmark — identify which driving schools ARE showing up in AI answers for our market, and break down why. What are they doing that we're not? What sources are LLMs citing about them?
Citation gap analysis — what sources do AI engines cite when discussing our niche (driving schools, learner permits, road tests, driving education in Canada)? Where should our brand realistically appear in those source streams, and how do we get there?
Site audit — full review of our website for AI-readability: schema markup, structured data, content extractability, FAQ structure, entity signals, knowledge graph alignment, semantic SEO foundations.
Action plan with priorities — a clear, prioritized roadmap of what we need to do. Not a vague "add more schema." We want specifics: which schema types, which content gaps to fill, which third-party sources we need to appear in, what content to create, what to restructure, and which fixes will move the needle fastest.
Full written report — delivered as a PDF or structured document we can hand to our team and execute against.

What We're NOT Looking For

Surface-level audits that just say "you're missing FAQ schema" — we want depth and reasoning
Generic SEO advice that doesn't address AI search specifically
AI-generated reports with no real expertise behind them
Freelancers who don't understand the difference between traditional SEO, AEO, and GEO

We want someone who genuinely understands how LLMs source, weight, and surface information — and can teach us through the report itself, not just deliver a checklist.
To Apply, Please Include

Your quote for the full audit
Your portfolio — specifically, which sites you've done GEO work for, what the starting position was, what you did, and what the outcome was
Your approach — briefly, how do you actually run a GEO audit? What tools, what process, what makes your audit different from someone running a generic SEO scan?
Estimated turnaround for the full report
One quick observation about our market or niche (driving schools in Canada) and how AI search engines typically handle local service businesses like ours — this helps us see how you think before we share the URL

About Us
Established driving school in Canada, multiple instructors, serving learner drivers preparing for road tests. We have a working website, decent traditional SEO, but we know AI search is the next frontier and we want to get ahead of it before our competitors do.
If this audit goes well and the recommendations are solid, we'll likely come back to you to actually implement the fixes — so this is also a chance to start a longer relationship.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.title: SEO / GEO Professional Content Writer
upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Overview
We're a behavioral health-focused EHR and practice management platform built exclusively for mental health and substance use disorder practices, from solo therapists to large multi-site organizations.

We help behavioral health practitioners focus their efforts, speed their process, and track their progress through purpose-built clinical, billing, and patient experience tools.

We're looking for a skilled freelance content writer to join our marketing team on an ongoing contract basis. You'll produce long-form, polished, data-informed content that drives organic search visibility, supports our full-funnel marketing strategy, and increasingly satisfies the emerging requirements of generative engine optimization (GEO): content built to perform inside AI-powered search experiences like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. We're not looking for volume alone; we're looking for quality, consistency, and a writer who takes behavioral health seriously.

What You'll Write
Long-form blog and thought leadership articles (1,500–2,000 words) targeting behavioral health practice owners, clinicians, practice managers, billers, and operations leads. Topics will span clinical documentation, billing and reimbursement, practice growth, compliance, IOP/PHP program management, measurement-based care, telehealth, and EHR selection. You'll receive briefs for most assignments, but strong writers who can develop angles independently will have more opportunities here.

Content will be written for full-funnel use (TOFU, MOFU, BOFU), so you should be equally comfortable writing educational explainers and more conversion-oriented comparison or solution-focused pieces.

What We're Looking For
You have demonstrated experience writing long-form SEO content for B2B SaaS, healthcare technology, or behavioral/mental health audiences. You understand how to build articles around keyword intent, not just keyword density. You're familiar with how modern search, including AI search, evaluates authority, entity coverage, semantic depth, and source credibility.

You write in a way that respects the reader's intelligence. Behavioral health practitioners are busy, highly trained professionals. They need clear, useful, well-sourced content that makes a real difference in how they run their practices.

You're comfortable working with a style guide and brand voice. You don't need heavy editing to produce publish-ready copy.

GEO Awareness
In addition to traditional SEO best practices which we’ll share our own documentation on, we're increasingly focused on GEO: writing content structured to be cited, summarized, or surfaced by AI search tools.

This means clear factual statements, well-defined entity relationships, authoritative sourcing, structured answers to specific questions, and content that builds topical authority rather than chasing individual keywords. If you're not already thinking about content this way, we'd like you to be.

Brand Voice
Our voice is collaborative, insightful, and results-focused. Our customers are the heroes of the story. We provide tools and context that help them succeed.

Our content shouldn't tell practitioners what to do in a prescriptive, authoritarian way. It should position the reader as a capable expert with access to better information and better tools.

Tone is professional but not clinical, warm but not casual. We avoid jargon-as-filler and overly salesy language. We acknowledge that behavioral health is nuanced and our content should reflect that.

Write in second person ("you can," "your practice") rather than passive or third-person constructions. Active voice throughout. Straightforward sentences.

Practical Requirements
Each article will be 1,500–2,000 words. Deliverables include the body copy, a suggested meta title and meta description, and suggested header structure if not already provided in the brief. Inline source citations or a reference list should be included where data, statistics, or clinical claims are made. Images and design are handled by our team; you focus on content and substance.

We expect clean first drafts. We'll provide feedback if revisions are needed, but we're not looking to rewrite submissions from scratch.

Turnaround is typically 5–7 business days from brief delivery, though we're flexible on specific deadlines when there's advance notice.

Subject Matter Familiarity (Strongly Preferred)
You don't have to be a clinician, but ideally you have some working knowledge of the behavioral health space or a track record writing for healthcare SaaS audiences. Familiarity with terms like PHQ-9, IOP/PHP, CPT codes, ePrescribing, measurement-based care, PDMP, or value-based care is a plus. If you're not already fluent in these, you should be a fast and thorough researcher who can credibly write about them after a brief.

Compensation
This is a per-article contract engagement. Rates are flexible and negotiated based on experience, writing sample quality, and proven results. 

Writers at the higher end of our range are expected to require minimal briefing, deliver publish-ready drafts, and bring strategic thinking to topics beyond what's in the brief. Volume and long-term availability are factors in rate discussions.

To Apply
Please submit two to three writing samples most relevant to this work. B2B SaaS, healthcare technology, or behavioral health strongly preferred.

A brief note about your experience with SEO and/or GEO content strategy is helpful. We don’t need a cover letter, but we do read what you write, so treat your application message as a writing sample in its own right.

We're a lean marketing team that values responsiveness and directness. If you've read this far and feel like a strong fit, say so plainly and show us your work.

Full technical SEO audit and implementation — site structure, meta tags, schema markup, page speed, mobile optimisation

Google Search Console and Analytics setup and configuration
Initial blog content calendar — minimum 12 topics mapped to high-intent keywords
Internal linking strategy across the site
Local and national citation setup where relevant

2–4 SEO-optimised blog articles per month (written or briefed, to be discussed)
Monthly keyword ranking report with actionable recommendations
Ongoing technical SEO monitoring and fixes
Backlink strategy and outreach for domain authority building
Quarterly content strategy review aligned with active investment corridors


Ideal Candidate

3+ years of SEO experience with demonstrable ranking results
Prior experience in financial services, real estate, or investment verticals preferred
Strong understanding of YMYL SEO best practices
Ability to write or brief authoritative long-form content — not generic filler
Proficient with Ahrefs or SEMrush, Google Search Console, Screaming Frog or equivalent
Self-directed — able to operate with minimal hand-holding

Agencies or large teams — this is a focused freelance engagement
Black-hat or grey-hat link building approaches
Generic content writers repurposed as SEO consultants
Anyone who cannot show verified ranking results from previous work


Engagement Terms

Phase 1 setup: project basis — scope and fees to be discussed
Phase 2 retainer: monthly — scope and fees to be discussed
Remote engagement — India-based preferred
Reporting directly to BWG leadership


To Apply
Share your portfolio, two to three case studies with ranking results, and a brief note on why you are the right fit for a firm operating in the investment and land acquisition space.

Job Title: Simple Automated SEO Audit Tool (Generate PDF Report & Capture Email)

Job Type: One-time project / Fixed price

150
–

Description:

I need a simple, automated SEO audit tool for my AI SEO agency. The goal is NOT a complex SaaS platform, but a functional script/web tool that:

Accepts a user’s website URL and email address on a simple form.

Runs a basic SEO audit (scrapes only public data – no login required).

Generates a clean, branded PDF report (max 2-3 pages).

Automatically emails that PDF to the lead’s email address (and BCCs me).

Saves the lead’s email + URL + timestamp to a simple Google Sheet or CSV (for my email list).

Required audit metrics (keep it simple/low cost):

Page title length & keyword presence

Meta description length

H1 tag presence

Image alt text count (present/missing)

Basic mobile-friendly check (viewport tag)

Page load speed (just a simple score from an API like PageSpeed Insights, if possible within budget – otherwise skip speed)

List of top 3 on-page issues with plain English recommendations

Technical preferences (cheapest option):

PHP + JavaScript (shared hosting friendly) OR

Python (Flask) + free tier hosting suggestion, OR

Node.js if cheap to deploy

What I will provide:

Logo + brand colors for PDF header

One sample PDF layout (hand-drawn or described)

SMTP credentials for sending email

What I do NOT need:

No user login / dashboard

No database (Google Sheet is fine)

No complex crawling beyond 1 page per audit

No payment integration

No scraping that violates ToS

Deliverables:

Working code (zipped) with setup instructions

Simple install on my cPanel or free hosting (e.g., Render, Replit, or 000webhost)

One Google Sheet integration working

PDF generation working with sample data

Ideal freelancer:

Has built similar lead-gen tools before

Can recommend free/low-cost APIs (e.g., Google PageSpeed free tier)

Speaks decent English

Can finish within 5–7 days

Fixed price: $200 (firm – budget is tight)

To apply: Show me one SEO or lead-gen automation tool you’ve built (even a simple one). Do not bid over $250.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Job Description:

About us
We are a full-service digital agency combining deep expertise in UX design, UI, branding, web development, SEO, answer engine optimization (AEO), structured data, AI search, accessibility, and digital marketing. Our clients range from small local businesses to established brands across the United States and Europe, and include names such as Google, Deutsche Bank, Leica, and McAfee. We are now expanding our sales network and looking for senior representatives who can bring our services to businesses in their area.

The role

You will identify and approach small and mid-sized businesses that could benefit from any of our services, from a new website or brand identity to SEO, UX improvements, or speed optimization. You do not need to be a technical expert. Your job is to open doors, build trust, and understand what the business needs. Our team handles the technical conversations, proposals, and closes the contract directly with the client.
Once a client is onboard, you remain their primary point of contact for day-to-day communication, basic support, and ongoing relationship management. You will also be positioned to identify upsell opportunities as the relationship grows.

Why this works for you

Our service catalog is broad, which means you can approach almost any business with a genuine solution. You are not selling one product to a narrow audience. A local restaurant might need a website and branding. A law firm might need SEO and accessibility compliance. A retailer might need UX improvements and speed optimization. Every conversation has potential.
Commission is paid on new contracts and on all recurring monthly fees for as long as the client stays active. A portfolio of 15 to 20 recurring clients generates substantial passive monthly income that grows independently of new sales activity.

Compensation

Retainer plus performance-based commission. Base commission starts at 10% on all new and recurring contracts and scales to 20% based on portfolio size and sustained performance. There is no ceiling on portfolio size.

Requirements

Minimum 3 years of B2B sales experience, preferably in digital services, marketing, web, or agency environments. Strong ability to build long-term trust with small business owners. Based in the United States or Western Europe. An existing local or regional business network is a strong advantage. No technical background required. All representatives go through a structured onboarding program that includes video classes, webinars, written documentation, and ongoing training, so you can speak confidently about our services from day one without being an expert in any of them, though familiarity with digital services is a plus.

Payments & platform policy

All payments are processed exclusively through Upwork, without exception. We do not operate outside the platform under any circumstance. Upwork's service fees are fully absorbed by us and are already factored into our commission structure, so the percentage you receive is your net take-home with no deductions on your end beyond standard Upwork withdrawal costs.

About the budget

The fixed-price amount listed is a placeholder required by the platform and does not reflect actual compensation. This is a commission-based role. Real earnings are outlined in the Compensation section above. Please do not apply based on the posted budget figure, you'd actually be able to get paid much more than that.

Who this is for

This is a strong fit for highly motivated individuals looking to build a recurring income stream, as well as for agencies or freelancers who already have an established client base and are looking to expand their portfolio with premium, high-value digital services. If you work with small and mid-sized businesses and are currently unable to offer UX, SEO, or full-stack digital services in-house, this is a natural extension of what you already do. White label arrangements are also available for agencies that prefer to offer these services under their own brand.

upwork-vibe~upwork-job-scraper.description:
Make.com Automation: AI Content App → YouTube Pipeline

Project Overview

We are an institutional capital advisory firm publishing 3-4 short-form video essays per day to YouTube as part of an AI search optimization (AEO) content strategy. 

Our content generation app is already built and producing fully structured JSON outputs ready for downstream automation. We need a Make.com automation specialist to build the delivery pipeline from app output to published YouTube video.

This is a **fixed-price starter project**. Successful delivery leads to an **ongoing $1,200/month automation retainer** for additional workflow builds (CRM routing, LP database enrichment, content distribution automation).

What You Are Building

A single Make.com scenario that receives a structured webhook payload from our content app and ends with a scheduled YouTube video, a logged Notion record, and a Slack notification.

Input Schema

The scenario receives a webhook POST with this exact JSON structure in the attachment.

Note: the `slides` and `script_sections` arrays are 1:1 aligned by `slide_number`. Each video typically contains 10-15 slides (variable based on content length). Your scenario must loop dynamically through these arrays without hard-coding count.

Pipeline Steps

1. **Receive webhook payload** — parse and validate all fields exist
2. **Concatenate narration** — join all `script_sections[].narration_text` into a single string with appropriate pauses between sections
3. **Generate voiceover via ElevenLabs API** — single API call returning one audio file using provided voice ID
4. **Build Creatomate render request** — pass voiceover URL + slides array (looping through all slides, mapping headline/subtext to corresponding template elements, using entry_timestamp for slide display timing)
5. **Submit render to Creatomate** — use webhook callback for completion (no sleep timers)
6. **Generate thumbnail** — second Creatomate template renders thumbnail from `youtube_title` + branded background
7. **Upload to YouTube via YouTube Data API v3** — set as private with `publishAt` field equal to `target_publish_slot`, attach thumbnail, attach pre-formatted description and tags
8. **Update Notion database** — write row with status "Published," YouTube URL, render timestamp, publish timestamp, video_id
9. **Send Slack notification** — include YouTube URL and scheduled publish time
10. **Error handling** — any failed step writes detailed error to Notion row with status "Error - [step name]" and posts Slack alert with diagnostic info

Deliverables

- Working Make.com scenario, fully tested with sample payloads
- Documented Creatomate `modifications` payload structure (which slide JSON fields map to which template element names)
- Documented Notion database schema (you specify required fields; we create the database)
- 15-minute Loom walkthrough of the scenario for handoff
- One successful end-to-end test render published to YouTube

Budget and Milestones

**Budget: $300-400 fixed depending on proposed approach.** Stronger track record on similar Make + Creatomate builds justifies the higher end.

Split into three milestones via Upwork:

 **Milestone 1 (35% of total)** — Make scenario receives webhook, parses JSON payload correctly, generates voiceover via ElevenLabs, and renders one test slide via Creatomate. Demonstrated via Loom.

**Milestone 2 (40% of total)** — Full video renders end-to-end with voiceover synced across all slides in the payload, thumbnail generated, render completes successfully. Demonstrated via Loom with a 12+ slide test payload.

**Milestone 3 (25% of total)** — YouTube upload with scheduled publish time + Notion logging + Slack notification working. One complete production-equivalent video published. Loom handoff.

Required From Applicants

Three things, no exceptions. Proposals without all three will be rejected without review.

1. **Loom video (3-5 minutes)** walking through a similar Make.com automation you have built that includes Creatomate or another video render API, plus at least one of (ElevenLabs, YouTube Data API v3, or Notion API).

2. **One paragraph (4-6 sentences)** explaining how you would structure the Creatomate `modifications` payload to handle a variable-length array of slides (10-15) with synchronized text and timing changes against a single audio track. Reference specific property naming conventions, dynamic duration handling, and how the scenario loops through the slides array without hard-coding count.

3. **Confirmation** that you understand the milestone structure and are willing to deliver Milestone 1 within 3 business days of contract start.

Tools and Access We Provide

- ElevenLabs API key + voice ID
- Creatomate API key + pre-built slide and thumbnail templates
- YouTube channel access (OAuth setup we complete jointly)
- Notion API token + database access
- Make.com Pro account (we cover any operation overages)
- Sample webhook payloads from our content app for development

Timeline

10 business days from contract start to Milestone 3 completion.

About Us

IRC Partners is a capital advisory firm publishing institutional-grade research content daily. We are scaling automated content distribution as a major growth initiative through 2026. 

Successful contractors on this project become preferred partners for future builds across our content, CRM, and prospect intake workflows.
